title: Treatment Outcomes and Molecular Prognostic Factors in TP53 Mutated Myeloid Neoplasms
official: Treatment Outcomes and Molecular Prognostic Factors in TP53 Mutated Myeloid Neoplasms
summary: TP53-mutated myeloid neoplasms encompass biologically heterogeneous disorders with frequent cytogenetic abnormalities and poor outcomes. In myelodysplastic neoplasms, TP53 allelic state contributes to clinical phenotype and prognosis. In acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes with excess blasts, molecular similarities support studying TP53-associated disease across conventional diagnostic boundaries, although pooling lower-risk and advanced diseases can introduce important clinical heterogeneity. Available therapies improve remission in some patients without reliably producing durable disease control. In a pooled analysis of poor-risk cytogenetic AML with TP53 mutations, azacitidine plus venetoclax increased remission compared with azacitidine alone without a corresponding improvement in survival. A recent molecular analysis of the pivotal CPX-351 trial found that benefit was concentrated in AML with myelodysplasia-related mutations rather than TP53-mutated AML. Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) can provide prolonged survival in selected patients, but its outcome depends on biological and clinical context. Retrospective transplant data support integrating VAF and cytogenetics, whereas biological-assignment data in MDS suggest that some patients with TP53 mutations benefit from transplantation. the investigators sought to describe treatment patterns and outcomes in a pooled TP53-associated clinical cohort and to explore cytogenetic abnormalities, TP53 mutation burden, co-mutation presence, and VAF. A secondary objective was to describe transplanted patients according to available pre-HCT TP53 VAF and to assess HCT as a time-dependent exposure. Our purpose was hypothesis generation rather than causal ranking of regimens or derivation of a validated transplant-selection rule.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* TP53 mutated myeloid AML (\> 20% blasts) or HR-SMD
* Age: Age ≥ 18 years
* Allo-HCT was permitted.
* Available NGS analysis at diagnosis
* TP53 VAF \> 2%
* Myeloid sarcoma were permitted
* Patients received at least 1 treatment line

Exclusion Criteria:

* TP53 mutations class 1 or 2 or 3 (American College of Medical Genetic and Genomics
* Patients alive at the start of the study who did not receive study information or who objected to the collection of data
* TP53 CCUS or CHIP
